#The generic Odin ABI for the engine boundary

Status: in use for one domain (URL / URLSearchParams in the engine, native/js/odin/web_url.odin); the standalone trunk native/js/odin_abi/ proves every shape on both paths. The plan is Sacha's of 28/10 ("GARDER LE WASM"): the engine stays a Wasm module, the boundary becomes a small generic ABI whose bridges the compiler instantiates from shared Odin declarations, with no code generator; the only tool left extracts documentation and conformance.

#The pieces

native/js/odin_abi/
  abi/          abi.odin apply.odin marshal.odin wire.odin invoke.odin   -- shapes, cells, apply, the codecs
  api_decl/     url.odin abitest.odin                                    -- the shared declarations
  abi_host/     host.odin dispatch.odin scalar.odin                      -- host bridges: bind (serialised), register_scalar
  abi_guest/    guest.odin host_call.odin guest_url.odin guest_abitest.odin -- the guest's serialised stubs
  abi_url/      host.odin impl.odin abitest.odin                         -- a standalone URL host (real wb:url)
  check/        in-process round trip of every shape, serialised
  bench/ bench_guest/  Wasmtime runner + wasm32 guest: scalar vs serialised vs hand-written, and scalar == serialised
  apidoc/       docs/conformance from api_decl (core:odin/parser)
native/js/odin/jsb/   the JavaScript side inside the engine: JS values <-> declaration types, lowering onto wr_* imports

#Declarations (package api_decl)

One package both ends import. A declaration is a procedure type: the arguments and the results, nothing else.

Odin
URL :: distinct abi.Handle                       // a handle kind: named after its interface
URLComponent :: enum i32 { Href, Protocol, ... }
URL_get :: #type proc(url: URL, component: URLComponent) -> (string, abi.Api_Error)
URLPattern_create :: #type proc(init: URLPatternInit) -> (URLPattern, abi.Api_Error)   // a dictionary argument
Abi_Make :: #type proc(href: string) -> (abi.Owned(URL), abi.Api_Error)               // the caller releases

The shapes the boundary carries (abi.Shape):

shapeOdin typescalar wire (today's wr_*)serialised wire
bool / i32 / enumbool, an integer of 4 bytes or less, enum i32one i324 bytes (bool: 1)
i64 / handle / Ownedi64, u64, distinct abi.Handle, abi.Owned(H)one i648 bytes
floatf32, f64one f32 / f644 / 8 bytes
string / bytesstring (UTF-8 checked), abi.Bytes / []u8(ptr, len)u32 length + bytes
optional spanMaybe(string), Maybe(Bytes)(ptr, len), len = ABSENT when absentlength ABSENT when absent
optional scalarMaybe(T)(present i32, value)u8 flag + value
slice[]T(ptr, count)u32 count + the elements
dictionarya structserialised onlyits fields in declaration order (any shape above, nested)

Results: nothing; a value; abi.Api_Error; (value, abi.Api_Error). On the scalar wire a string result is a (buffer, capacity) pair after the arguments and the return is the full length (negative: the error); a (value, error) result is one more parameter, the address the value is stored at, and the return is the status; an absent Maybe(string) result is Not_Found.

#The bridges, comptime

Everything reduces to two steps.

  1. Decode the arguments, from wherever they arrive, into one abi.Cell per declared parameter (a scalar in a; a span a = address, b = length; an optional with its marker). Each source is a compile-time recursion over the declaration's parameter types (proc(..., $P: typeid, $i, $n: int), intrinsics.type_proc_parameter_type(P, i) with i constant), one specialised step per parameter:

    • abi_host.register_scalar: the raw cells of a Wasm call (bounds-checked spans, UTF-8 check);
    • abi.decode_params: a serialised buffer (dictionaries through a run-time type-information walk, the cold path);
    • jsb.args: the JSValues of a JS call (wj_to_str / web_to_usv, wj_to_int32, wj_to_handle...).
  2. Apply the procedure: abi.apply(cells, P, p, &r0, &r1). Odin can walk a procedure type at compile time but cannot build a call of variable arity, so apply is the one place where arities 0..16 are spelled out; it serves every source and every return shape.

The wire shape of a scalar import (its Wasm parameter list) is filled by the same recursion as its decoding, so they cannot disagree. A binding is proved against its declaration at compile time:

  • abi.must_bind(Decl, Impl) (host): Impl is Decl plus a leading context, same results;
  • abi.must_match(Decl, Stub) (guest stubs);
  • jsb's lowering asserts that the generated import has the declaration's wire shape (a span is a pointer then a 4-byte length, a string result two more parameters, a (value, error) result one address). Two imports of the same shape (URL_get and URL_set are both (u64, i32, ptr, u32) -> i32) cannot be told apart by types; the name in the binding is the remaining guarantee.

Each failure is a compile error naming the parameter (a where clause on a constant index).

#Measurements

1 M calls, wasm32 guest over Wasmtime (Cranelift), best of five batches (the machine is shared: a median of three moved by 2x between runs), native/js/odin_abi/bench, 28/10:

shapewr_* scalar (hand-written)scalar bridge (comptime)serialised host_call (comptime)
URLSearchParams_size (handle -> i32)5.4 ns7.7 ns34.1 ns
URL_get .Pathname (handle, enum -> string)32.3 ns33.1 ns71.1 ns
URLSearchParams_has (handle, string, Maybe(string) -> bool)20.0 ns30.1 ns81.2 ns
Abi_Mix8 (i32 i64 f64 bool enum string Maybe(string) handle -> i64)-33.5 ns119.3 ns

Readings:

  • The comptime scalar bridge is the generated trampoline, plus 2–10 ns: the embedder's begin/end and the UTF-8 check go through function pointers (the hand-written baseline calls nothing for size and validates inline for has). With eight mixed arguments it stays at ~34 ns.
  • The serialised path costs ~+30–90 ns (one copy per argument, a dispatch through the op table): constructors, dictionaries, cold functions; not the hot getters.
  • Inside the engine, a URL getter bound through jsb (url.pathname 200 000 times in a page) costs ~205 ns against ~190 ns for the hand-written port: +15 ns for the cells and the generic this.

bench also checks that every shape gives the same answer through the scalar bridge and the serialised path (check_shapes), and check verifies the serialised answers against the expected values in process.

#Inside the engine: jsb

The engine reaches the host through the generated wr_* imports (native/js/odin/wj/wr_imports.odin). jsb binds a WebIDL member to a declaration and the import that carries it, with no per-function code:

Odin
jsb.getter(ctx, this_val, api_decl.URL_get, wj.wr_URL_get, URLComponent.Pathname, "URL")      // an attribute
jsb.method(ctx, this_val, argc, argv, api_decl.URLSearchParams_toString, wj.wr_URLSearchParams_toString, "URLSearchParams.toString")
jsb.function(ctx, argc, argv, api_decl.URL_canParse, wj.wr_URL_canParse, "URL.canParse", .USV)  // static
jsb.host(&count, api_decl.URLSearchParams_count, wj.wr_URLSearchParams_count, p, name)          // from behaviour code

this is the declaration's first parameter (its interface comes from the handle kind's name); the JS arguments are converted by the declaration's types (a trailing Maybe is optional, the arity error is computed); the declaration is lowered onto the import (strings to (ptr, len), Maybe(string) to WR_ABSENT, the string-result buffer grown and retried once, the (value, error) address); the result goes back to JS by type, an Api_Error throws (wj_throw_status).

#How to migrate a domain (10 steps)

The example is web_url (commit bdd9a031): 327 lines with every host call typed by hand, 256 lines with none.

  1. Read the domain and sort it. In the ported native/js/odin/<domain>.odin (or the .c), mark what only carries a call across (category A: getters, setters, numeric calls, toString), what adapts (B: defaults, optional arguments, dictionaries), and what is behaviour (C: caches, sequences and records, iterators, bespoke messages).
  2. Declare. For each host function the domain calls, write its declaration in native/js/odin_abi/api_decl/<module>.odin from api/<module>.widl: handle kinds as distinct abi.Handle named after their interface, enums i32, raises as an abi.Api_Error last result (a string getter that fails on a released handle raises), ownership as abi.Owned(H), a dictionary as a struct.
  3. Check the wire. The generated import wj.wr_<Name> must be the declaration's lowering (the table in "Shapes"). jsb asserts it when you bind; a mismatch is the declaration being wrong, not the import.
  4. Replace the pass-through members by one line each: jsb.getter (an attribute selected by a constant), jsb.method (this + JS arguments), jsb.function (static / global). Choose .USV where the IDL says USVString. The error text is what: keep the C's ("URL", "URLSearchParams.toString").
  5. Rewrite behaviour on jsb.host. Every remaining host call becomes jsb.host(&out, api_decl.X, wj.wr_X, args...): the operand structs, fill callbacks, WJ_FETCH_STRING loops, (ptr, len) / WR_ABSENT lowering and status checks disappear. A string result lives in the scratch buffer until the next host call: convert it first.
  6. Replace this checks and interface caches by jsb.this(ctx, this_val, Kind) and jsb.iface_of(Kind).
  7. Keep the exported names. Every wjr_* the generated binding table references stays @(export, link_name = ...) with the same signature; nothing changes in native/js/gen.
  8. Build and check: odin check native/js/odin -target:freestanding_wasm32 -no-entry-point -default-to-nil-allocator -vet, then cmd /c build.bat.
  9. Test what the domain touches: jstest, the e2e tool of the domain (jswebtest for url), tools\wpt.ps1 -Only /<folder>/ -TimeoutMs 30000. The judge is "the same subtests pass as before", against a build of the commit before the migration when wpt/expectations is older than the code.
  10. Measure the hot members (a page timing 200 000 calls, wren ctl run --eval), report the before/after, commit.

Before (hand-typed transmission, one of each kind):

Odin
@(private = "file") Comp_Op :: struct { handle: u64, component: i32 }
@(private = "file")
fill_url_get :: proc "contextless" (user: rawptr, buf: [^]u8, cap: u32) -> i32 {
	op := (^Comp_Op)(user)
	return wj.wr_URL_get(op.handle, op.component, buf, cap)
}
@(private = "file")
url_get :: proc "c" (ctx: ^wj.Context, this_val: wj.JSValue, component: i32) -> wj.JSValue {
	h, ok := url_handle(ctx, this_val)
	if !ok { return wj.EXCEPTION }
	op := Comp_Op{ h, component }
	n := wj.fetch_string(fill_url_get, &op)
	if n < 0 { return wj.wj_throw_status(ctx, n, "URL") }
	return wj.new_string_len(ctx, wj.scratch_bytes(n))
}
@(export, link_name = "wjr_URL_get_href") wjr_URL_get_href :: proc "c" (ctx: ^wj.Context, t: wj.JSValue) -> wj.JSValue { return url_get(ctx, t, URLC_HREF) }

url_parse :: proc "c" (input: ^wj.Str, base: ^wj.Str, status: ^i32) -> u64 {
	h := u64(0)
	base_len := base.ptr != nil ? u32(base.len) : WR_ABSENT
	status^ = wj.wr_URL_parse(input.ptr, u32(input.len), base.ptr, base_len, &h)
	return status^ < 0 ? 0 : h
}

After:

Odin
@(export, link_name = "wjr_URL_get_href") wjr_URL_get_href :: proc "c" (ctx: ^wj.Context, t: wj.JSValue) -> wj.JSValue { return get(ctx, t, .Href) }
// with, once for the ten components:
get :: #force_inline proc "contextless" (ctx: ^wj.Context, t: wj.JSValue, component: URLComponent) -> wj.JSValue {
	return jsb.getter(ctx, t, api_decl.URL_get, wj.wr_URL_get, component, "URL")
}

url_parse :: proc(input: wj.Str, base: wj.Str) -> URL {
	u: URL
	b: Maybe(string) = base.ptr != nil ? str_of(base) : nil
	if jsb.host(&u, api_decl.URL_parse, wj.wr_URL_parse, str_of(input), b) != .None { return 0 }
	return u
}

#The host side, next

The host still serves module url through the bindgen trampolines (src/page/api_generated.odin). The same declarations bind its implementations with abi_host.register_scalar (the wire is identical, so the engine does not change): move src/page's URL implementations to the declaration's shape (proc(c: ^Call, <arguments>) -> <results>), register them, and drop the module from bindgen's host emitter. abi_url is that binding, standalone.

#What stays out of the comptime bridge

  • WebIDL overloads and unions (foo(DOMString) / foo(long), (DOMString or Blob)): resolved in the JS binding, by hand, dispatching to differently named declarations.
  • Callbacks (a listener handed to the host): a function-table index (wj.table_index) and a user word, unchanged.
  • Same-shape imports (two declarations whose lowering is identical): only the name tells them apart.
  • Enums from JS: a WebIDL enum is a string in JS; jsb does not convert it (a member takes it by hand, or the declaration takes a string).
